requirements.quote:
A client
   therefore MUST NOT use 0-RTT for application data unless specifically
   requested by the application that is in use.
requirements.condition: When an application has not specifically requested that its application data use 0-RTT
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client sends application data using 0-RTT.
requirements.why_checkable: A client API test can omit application authorization and inspect outgoing 0-RTT packets for application-data frames.

requirements.quote:
An application protocol that uses QUIC MUST include a profile that
   defines acceptable use of 0-RTT
requirements.condition: When an application protocol uses QUIC
requirements.required_behavior: Define a protocol profile specifying acceptable uses of 0-RTT.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit a profile defining the protocol's acceptable use of 0-RTT.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's application-protocol integration can be checked for an explicit 0-RTT policy/profile before application data is enabled in 0-RTT.

requirements.quote:
otherwise, 0-RTT can only be used to
   carry QUIC frames that do not carry application data.
requirements.condition: When the application protocol has no profile defining acceptable use of 0-RTT
requirements.required_behavior: Use 0-RTT only for QUIC frames that carry no application data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Carry an application-data-bearing QUIC frame in 0-RTT.
requirements.why_checkable: A no-profile test can decode every emitted 0-RTT frame and determine whether any carries application data.

requirements.quote:
A TLS handshake cannot be successfully completed using
   replayed packets.
requirements.condition: When an attacker or test peer supplies only replayed packets from an earlier exchange
requirements.required_behavior: Prevent the replayed packets from successfully completing the TLS handshake.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept the replay alone as a successfully completed TLS handshake.
requirements.why_checkable: A captured handshake flight can be replayed into a fresh connection and the endpoint's handshake completion state observed.

requirements.quote:
A client SHOULD stop sending 0-RTT data
   if it receives an indication that 0-RTT data has been rejected.
requirements.condition: When a client receives an indication that its 0-RTT data was rejected
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continue emitting new 0-RTT data without a justified exception to the SHOULD.
requirements.why_checkable: A server can reject 0-RTT and the subsequent client packet trace can be checked for additional 0-RTT data.

requirements.quote: A server MUST NOT use 0-RTT keys to protect packets
requirements.condition: When a server protects an outgoing QUIC packet
requirements.why_checkable: Server packets can be captured and tested against the server's 0-RTT and 1-RTT protection keys to identify the key level used.

requirements.quote:
it uses 1-RTT
   keys to protect acknowledgments of 0-RTT packets.
requirements.condition: When a server protects a packet carrying an acknowledgment of a 0-RTT packet
requirements.why_checkable: The acknowledgment-bearing packet can be decrypted with candidate traffic keys to verify that the server used the 1-RTT key set.

requirements.quote:
A client MUST NOT
   attempt to decrypt 0-RTT packets it receives
requirements.condition: When a client receives a packet identified as 0-RTT
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Attempt to decrypt the received 0-RTT packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation can verify that reception of a 0-RTT packet at a client does not invoke a decryption operation.

requirements.condition: When a client receives a 0-RTT packet
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Pass the packet or its contents to further protocol or application processing.
requirements.error_behavior: Discard the packet without attempting decryption.
requirements.why_checkable: A client can be sent a 0-RTT packet and observed to ensure the packet is dropped and produces no downstream processing.

requirements.quote:
Once a client has installed 1-RTT keys, it MUST NOT send any more
   0-RTT packets.
requirements.why_checkable: A client trace can correlate the 1-RTT key-install event with packet encryption levels and assert that no later packet is 0-RTT.

requirements.quote:
any packets containing acknowledgments of
      |  0-RTT data cannot have packet protection removed by the client
      |  until the TLS handshake is complete.
requirements.condition: Before the TLS handshake is complete, when the client receives a packet containing acknowledgments of 0-RTT data
requirements.required_behavior: Defer removal of packet protection from that packet until handshake completion.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Remove the packet's protection before the TLS handshake completes.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver an acknowledgment-bearing 1-RTT packet before handshake completion and observe whether decryption is deferred until the completion transition.

requirements.quote:
The 1-RTT keys necessary
      |  to remove packet protection cannot be derived until the client
      |  receives all server handshake messages.
requirements.condition: Before the client has received all server handshake messages
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Derive the 1-RTT keys needed to remove packet protection.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake and key-derivation events can be ordered to verify that 1-RTT key derivation occurs only after all server handshake messages arrive.
